Good puzzle. My opinion is that this puzzle is more suited for the easy section, but see what others say about it.

Goal
 - Format all numbers as constants {{}}. Maybe the 'L' from "L-shape" too.
 - Specify that the top left cell has coordinate 0,0. This is in order to clarify what smallest row or column index means.
 - Perhaps the last line should be in the constraints rather than the goal

Input and Output
 - Reference this page for formatting syntax: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement#guidelines
  As an example: <<Line 1:>> An integer [[n]] representing the side length of the chessboard.
 - Format . and N as constants {{}}. Format [[n]] as a variable
 - The last line can be removed from both. 

Constraints
 - move "The board contains {{one}} knight." to the constraints
 - format numbers as {{}}, n as [[]].

Cases
 - Firstly, I think that the 'N' should be replaced with 'K' or '0' to avoid confusion with the variable n.
 - The tests and validators should be more similar. I'm sure 5DN1L will have a more clear idea than I, but my opinion is that the test and validators should begin in the same quadrant of the board, and both cases should match in whether the knight begins in the center or on a corner or edge of the board.
 - Include a test case for n=16.
 - More cases testing different positions in the board. Make sure those relative positions are represented in both the test and validator. Currently there are 3 tests where we start in the centre matched to validators where we start in a corner.

Stub generator
 - word(100) can be reduced to word(16).
 - Include a write statement. e.g. write the resulting board

Thank you so much for your comment! This is my first puzzle. I just had an interesting idea and wanted to give it a try. I tried to allow for multiple valid solutions, but couldn't figure out how to implement that, so I ended up defaulting to a rule where the smaller coordinate is always chosen. I'll definitely take your advice into account and work on fixing these issues. Thanks again!

First and foremost, please switch the puzzle's status to WIP first to avoid accidental approval.

@Sflubaduba has done an excellent review, so I won't repeat the points they've already covered 👍

Regarding the difficulty, this problem is a bit more involved than simple loops, conditionals or string manipulation, so I think Medium is an appropriate difficulty level.

Regarding the cases, @Sflubaduba has already outlined how the cases should be updated. Since it may be difficult to ensure that every test-validator case pair starts in the same quadrant, I'd suggest the following approach:

The following properties should match, or be as similar as reasonably possible, within each case pair:
* Parity of board size: odd or even
* Board size: preferably the same, or differing by 2
* Starting position category: corner, edge (excluding corners), at the centre (if applicable), or at a non-centre interior position

The above properties, together with starting quadrant, should appear the same number of times across all tests and, separately, across all validators, as far as possible.

Please also aim for variety in the starting positions based on their relative distance from the edges. For example, two starting positions can belong to the same quadrant but still represent different scenarios if one is closer to an edge and the other is farther away.

Finally, I suspect the tie-breaking rules are exercised in most cases, but if they aren't, please ensure that both row-based and column-based tie-breaking are covered by some case pairs.

Thanks.

Thank you for the detailed feedback! I've switched the puzzle to WIP. I also didn't fully understand the purpose of pairing tests with validators before, but now I understand how they should correspond and I'll work on making them more consistent. I'll also add more varied starting positions, a 16×16 test case, and make sure the tie-breaking rules are properly covered.

Glad to help!

Also, remember that you aren't limited to 4 pairs of cases; in fact, you'll need more case pairs to cover all possible combinations of quadrants and starting position categories 😉

As mentioned above,
* Input: Please format "Line 1" and "Next [[n]] lines" in bold.

* Input: Please format "." and "K" as {{constants}} instead of [[variables]].

* Output: Please change "Print the resulting chessboard as n lines, each" to "<<[[n]] lines>>: The resulting chessboard, each line".

* Output: Please format both instances of "n" in "n×n - 1" as a [[variable]].

* Cases: Please add more case pairs.

Parity: odd or even => 2
Board size: small or big => 2
Starting position category: corner, edge, centre, non-centre => 4 (+ non-centre can still be subdivided into near edge, near centre, and neither)
Starting quadrant => 4

2 x 2 x 4 x 4 = 64 combinations at a minimum

That means you should create all 25 case pairs to cover as many combinations as possible (and even then, you still won't cover every possibility).

Please switch back to WIP, and don't switch to Ready too soon after addressing the issues. Give others a chance to review the contribution and provide feedback first, especially since your previous comment suggested that you were still working on it.

Thanks.

Thank you for your feedback! I didn’t fully understand my mistakes before, but I hope I have a better understanding of them now.

I’ve made the changes you suggested, including fixing the formatting in the Input and Output sections and adding more case pairs to cover different combinations.

Unfortunately, I couldn’t add more than 25 case pairs because I kept getting the following error: Oops An error occurred (#542): "There are too many test cases". So I added the maximum number of pairs allowed.

I’ll leave the puzzle in WIP and wait for your review and approval before switching it to Ready. Thanks again for taking the time to point these things out!

Many thanks. The test case set is much more comprehensive now. There are a number of things to do to improve the variety and distribution of board sizes and starting positions.

I've revised the test cases and updated the input formatting according to your comments. I also reviewed the distribution of starting positions and the variety of board configurations to make the test suite more balanced.

I appreciate the time you've spent reviewing my puzzle and helping me improve it. I hope everything is correct now.

Thanks again for your time and patience!
